title: Standard Operating Procedure for Culture Identification and Differentiation of Bordetella species
author: Adria D. Lee
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.kvtcw6n

steps.title: Culture the Specimen
steps.instruction: Plate the NP specimen/isolate on RL+C and RL-C media and streak for isolation.

substeps.instruction: Incubate plates at 37°C for up to 10 days, checking daily.

steps.title: Identify and Subculture BLO Colonies
steps.instruction: Identify any Bordetella-like organism (BLO) on primary culture plates, noting that RL+C is most useful for B. pertussis and RL-C for B. holmesii.

substeps.instruction: If possible, plate a single BLO colony on RL-C and blood agar (BAP) using the same loop for both plates.
Streak these plates for isolation to ensure no contaminants are present.

steps.title: Evaluate Colony Morphology
steps.instruction: Observe colony appearance on Regan-Lowe and blood agar to differentiate species.

substeps.instruction: B. pertussis: Small, pearly white colonies on Regan-Lowe; pick and plate on RL-C for isolation (growth sufficient for testing after 3 days).
B. parapertussis: Similar to B. pertussis but grows faster (2-3 days on primary), not inhibited by cephalexin, larger colonies with slight brown pigment after 3-4 days.
B. bronchiseptica: Grows well on Regan-Lowe and blood agar after 1 day; not inhibited by cephalexin; colonies larger than B. pertussis with slight brown pigment on Regan-Lowe.
B. holmesii: Small, white colonies on Regan-Lowe (appears in 2-3 days); grows on blood agar but not well on agar containing cephalexin.

steps.title: Perform Gram Stain
steps.instruction: Gram stain growth from the blood agar and/or the secondary RL-C plate.

substeps.instruction: Verify the isolate consists of very small Gram negative short rods.
Compare with a Gram stain of a known B. pertussis for reference.
Discard the isolate if it is Gram positive (any shape), Gram negative cocci, or long rods.

steps.title: Perform Slide Agglutination
steps.instruction: If the Gram stain is correct, test the isolate by slide agglutination.

steps.title: Perform Biochemical Testing
steps.instruction: If the isolate is negative for B. pertussis and B. parapertussis, set up biochemical tests using growth from the blood agar plate (BAP).

substeps.instruction: Set up the following tests: Oxidase, Nitrate reduction, Urease, Motility, HIT agar slant, MacConkey, and Citrate.
Incubate biochemical tests at 37°C for 24 hours.

description: Limitations: Only acceptable specimens and suspected isolates of B. pertussis , B. parapertussis , B.holmesii and B. bronchiseptica should be tested with these protocols. Prior antibiotic treatment and/or vaccination with an anti-pertussis vaccine may interfere with recovery of B. pertussis from properly collected specimens. Failure to culture an isolate of B. pertussis does not necessarily mean the patient does not have pertussis.
